chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When something small falls into the well and dies in it, draw out buckets from it;
and if a sexually impure person (junub) falls into it, draw out seven buckets from it.
But if a camel dies in it, or wine is poured into it, then let it be completely emptied.

key_terms.البئر: Well — the primary communal water source in early Islamic society; well-purification rulings occupied a central place in classical Shia fiqh
key_terms.جنب: Junub — a person in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) requiring ghusl before prayer
key_terms.دلاء: Dila' (buckets) — the standard unit of measure for well purification; the exact count varied across narrations
key_terms.فلينزح: Let it be drawn out/emptied — the imperative form indicating a binding ruling for complete exhaustion of the well

ai.seo_question: How should a well be purified if something falls and dies in it according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) sets out graduated jurisprudential rulings for purifying a well contaminated by different causes. This hadith, transmitted through al-Halabi — one of the Imam's most authoritative students — reflects the practical fiqh questions that early Muslim communities faced regarding water sources. The three-tier ruling (a few buckets for a small dead creature, seven for a junub, complete emptying for a camel's carcass or wine) reflects principles of proportionality and severity in najasah (ritual impurity).
